input.quote: 13.4.1 Without the prior written consent of the other Party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, neither Party shall sell, transfer, assign, delegate, pledge, or otherwise dispose of, whether voluntarily, involuntarily, by operation of law or otherwise, this Agreement or any of its rights or duties hereunder; provided that either Party may make such an assignment without the other Party's consent to its Affiliate or to a successor, whether in a merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or any other transaction, of the business to which this Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 13.4.1 gives AbbVie an express right to assign without Harpoon's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, sale of stock or sale of assets of the relevant business, and makes consent for any other assignment subject to a "not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" standard — the preferred carve-out for our side. Nothing in Article 12 or elsewhere gives Harpoon a termination, re-pricing or other altered right on an AbbVie Change in Control; the only change-of-control machinery (Section 13.2, plus Sections 2.x and 5.x on a Harpoon Change in Control involving a Competitor) runs in our favour and requires Harpoon to notify us. Noted but not flagged: the clause is symmetrical, so Harpoon may likewise assign to an Affiliate/successor without our consent and there is no express bar on assignment to an AbbVie competitor; that is the playbook fallback (mutual successor assignment with consent otherwise not unreasonably withheld) and is acceptable, particularly given our separate competitor protections on a Harpoon Change in Control.
